sentences.english_text: The news broadcast of the President was carried live on television.
It happened that the wind was passing a television store that had a television set in its window.
The wind watched the news conference for a moment, and suddenly it saw Drippy on the President's shoe.
There he is.
Now I've got him.
The wind was not sure exactly where the press conference was taking place, so he blew himself high into the air where he could look down on the city.
There, just east of him, he saw the President and all the reporters.
The wind swooped down, and there was Drippy.
So, I've found you.
Hello, Mr. Wind.
Didn't I tell you to stay on the park bench?
And the wind's voice was so angry that Drippy was frightened.
He was afraid to tell the truth.
I fell off.
Drippy lied.
The wind stared at Drippy, and Drippy had no way of knowing whether the wind believed him or not.
Let's get out of here.
I hate press conferences.
And the wind picked Drippy up on his coattails, and away they went, up into the sky.
This is more like it.
Now I'm going to have another adventure.
Far, far below, down on the earth, Drippy's mother, Mrs. Dewdrop, was crying, because Drippy had been gone so long.
She was afraid he was dead.
Large, beautiful tears rolled out of her eyes, and down her cheeks and face.
And as the tears moved down, Mrs. Dewdrop moved with them, for she was made of tears, you see.
And in this way, she cried herself down the street, flowing along, like a tiny river.
